packages/dj-core/src/index.ts.content:
Non-positive `beatsPerSecond` collapses `errorMs` to `Infinity`, so `seek` is `true` for *every* observation of a paused/zero-tempo deck — even one with zero beat error.

This is reachable from production: `show-runtime`'s `tickWorld` builds the observation with `beatsPerSecond: state.playing ? tempoBps * state.playRate : 0` (packages/show-runtime/src/index.ts:641), so while a deck is paused `beatsPerSecond` is exactly `0`. After the cold-start observation, each subsequent paused tick computes `errorMs = Infinity > seekThresholdMs` -> `seeked: true`, which hard-resets `beat`/`rate`/`playing` and (in `tickWorld`) re-triggers the seek branch that clears `world.transients`/`world.cursor` and reports a transport event every frame. The existing "holds a paused deck" test masks this because it passes `beatsPerSecond: BEATS_PER_SECOND` instead of `0`.

Fix: only apply the millisecond threshold when the tempo is positive; a zero-tempo deck should be judged by the beat threshold alone.

`reset()` leaves the clock anchor and the motion state inconsistent. When `nowNs` is omitted (the default here, and also the default of `ShowRuntime.seek(deckId, beat)` -> `seekWorld(..., null)`), `lastNs` keeps its pre-seek value while `beat` jumps to the new position; `playing`/`rate` are likewise retained. The next `advance()`/`observe()` therefore extrapolates from the post-seek beat across the stale pre-seek interval at the pre-seek rate, and `advance()` itself is what feeds the non-fresh path in `tickWorld`, so the warped position can be consumed directly before any observation corrects it. A hard seek should re-anchor the clock (and, since the tempo/transport at the new location is unknown, not silently keep the old rate).

packages/matter/src/binding.test.ts.content: Cleanup is enqueued only after all assertions. If any `expect(...)` throws or `bindNode` unexpectedly resolves/rejects, `await adapter.close()` is never reached, so the adapter leaks and the cleanup failure can mask the real assertion failure. Move close into an `afterEach` (or wrap each test body in try/finally) so the adapter is always released.

This assertion only proves that an `identify/identify` command exists somewhere in the recorded command list; it does not validate the documented flow (flash → confirm → persist). Since reads are not recorded by InMemoryAdapter, a regression that runs `read(basicInformation)` after the identify command, or that writes the record before `confirmIdentify` resolves, would still pass. Assert the ordering explicitly (e.g. `commands.findIndex(...)` before any write, or inject/instrument `confirmIdentify` and check `commands`/`store` state at the moment it is invoked) rather than mere membership.

The test name claims the decline happens "after the flash", but nothing verifies a flash actually occurred, nor that the store was left untouched as a whole. A regression that skips the identify flash (e.g. confirms before flashing) or performs a partial write before rejecting would still pass. Add an assertion that the identify command was issued and that `store.size === 0`.

The rejected-rebind case only checks `matterNodeId`; it does not verify the stored record is otherwise unchanged (vendorId, productId, multiAdmin, boundAtMs) nor that no new identify/command side effects were emitted during the rejected attempt. A partial overwrite or a spurious flash on the rejected path would go undetected. Snapshot the full record before the attempt and assert `store.get("strip-3")` deep-equals it (and, if the flow intends the guard to run before flashing, that no extra command was recorded).

This block re-implements the same adapter/commission sequence as the `commissioned()` helper above instead of reusing it, so setup logic can drift from the commissioning contract. Consider extending/reusing the helper for the two-node setup.
packages/matter/src/binding.test.ts.existing_code:
const first = await adapter.commission("1234-567-8901", { source: "manual", provenance: "direct" });
    const second = await adapter.commission("MT:Y.K9042C00KA0648G00", { source: "scan", provenance: "multi-admin" });

packages/matter/src/mapping.ts.content: `clampByte` does not guard non-finite input: `Math.round(NaN)` is `NaN`, and `Math.max(0, Math.min(255, NaN))` is `NaN`. Nothing validates the `Rgb` fields, so a `NaN`/`Infinity` channel propagates through `rgbToHsl254` (hue 0, saturation `NaN`, level `NaN`), bypasses the black check in `toMatterWrites` (since `NaN !== 0`), and is emitted as `NaN` payload values on the wire. Coerce non-finite values (e.g. to 0) so invalid input cannot silently produce malformed writes.

HSL saturation is combined with a level derived from `max(r,g,b)` (the HSV value). These are different colour models, so for desaturated/pastel inputs the saturation is inflated: e.g. `{r:255,g:128,b:128}` yields HSL saturation `254` (fully saturated) even though HSV saturation is `127`. This makes on-device colours wrong if the target interprets saturation as HSV (the model that pairs with a max-channel level). Either use the HSV saturation (`range / max`) to match the level derivation, or document/verify the intended model.
packages/matter/src/mapping.ts.existing_code: const saturation = range === 0 ? 0 : range / (1 - Math.abs(2 * lightness - 1));

packages/matter/src/mapping.ts.content: `kelvin` and `level01` are not validated. `kelvin <= 0` produces `Infinity` (for 0) or a negative mireds that is silently clamped to 147/652, and a non-finite `kelvin`/`level01` yields `NaN` payloads (`Math.min(652, NaN) === NaN`). Invalid setup inputs therefore produce misleading commands instead of being rejected. Add finite/range validation (kelvin > 0, level01 within [0,1]) before computing.
packages/matter/src/mapping.ts.suggestion_code:
const safeKelvin = Number.isFinite(kelvin) && kelvin > 0 ? kelvin : 2700;
  const mireds = Math.max(147, Math.min(652, Math.round(1_000_000 / safeKelvin)));
packages/matter/src/mapping.ts.existing_code: const mireds = Math.max(147, Math.min(652, Math.round(1_000_000 / kelvin)));

packages/matter/src/mapping.ts.content: No guard against a zero or negative rate. `minIntervalMs(0)` returns `Infinity` and a negative rate returns a negative interval; the config key `govee.matter.commandRateHz` has no min constraint, so an unset/typo value can reach this helper and stall or mispace command output. Clamp to a sane positive floor (or throw) instead of returning `Infinity`/negative values.

The `onOff` 'on' + `levelControl` `moveToLevel` pair is duplicated verbatim in `toMatterWrites` and `cctToMatterSetupWrites`. Any change to the level/transition semantics must be applied in both places, which invites drift. Extract a small helper that builds these two writes.

packages/rekordbox-library/src/db.ts.content: Search input is wrapped as `%${search}%` without escaping LIKE metacharacters (`%`, `_`, and the escape char), so user text such as `100%`, `a_b` or `%%` broadens matches far beyond a literal substring. Worse, this diverges from the sidecar reader, whose `matchesSearch` uses a plain `String(...).includes()` comparison (sidecar.ts:335-340), so the same query returns different row sets (and a different `total`) depending on which reader is active — exactly what the DS-15 cross-check is meant to keep identical. Escape the wildcards and align both readers' semantics (or document the divergence).
packages/rekordbox-library/src/db.ts.existing_code: const SEARCH_WHERE = " WHERE c.Title LIKE :search OR ar.Name LIKE :search OR c.FolderPath LIKE :search";

packages/rekordbox-library/src/db.ts.content: Routing `Attribute` through `numberOrNull` means any non-`number` value (a TEXT-typed attribute column, a driver returning strings) collapses to `0`, so folders (1) and smart playlists (4) are silently reported as `"playlist"`. The `?? "playlist"` fallback also masks genuinely unknown attribute codes instead of surfacing them. Coerce the raw value directly and keep the fallback for truly unknown codes (or make unknown a distinct kind).

`text()` only accepts a real `string`; any numeric/BigInt ID (a driver or sidecar returning `ID`/`ContentID` as a number) is turned into the `""` fallback. `mapTrackRow`, `mapPlaylistRow`, `songPlaylistRows` and `historyTrackCounts` all use `text(row["id"], "")`, whereas `service.ts` and `sidecar.ts` consistently use `String(row["ID"] ?? "")`. That inconsistency makes the same row map to `""` here but `"101"` there, so `trackRow(id)` lookups and `tracksForEntries` membership resolution can silently return empty results for the TypeScript reader while the sidecar path works. Use `String(...)` (or extend `text()` to coerce numbers) for identity columns.

`numberOrNull` returns `null` for anything that is not a JS `number`. SQLite is dynamically typed, so numeric-looking columns can legitimately come back as strings (TEXT-declared columns such as BPM/Length/Rating/FileSize/SampleRate/BitRate/Seq/TrackNo) or as BigInt, and every such value is silently dropped to `null` rather than reporting a schema mismatch — the library would just show blank BPM/rating/duration with no error. Accept numeric strings/BigInt (e.g. coerce and reject non-finite results) or fail loudly on unexpected column types.

`historyTrackCounts` is only referenced by `db.test.ts`; it is not part of the `LibrarySource` interface (so `SidecarReader` has no equivalent) and `LibraryService.history()` computes the same count via a separate `songHistoryRows(...).length` path. This leaves two parallel counting implementations for the same data, one of which is unreachable from production code. Either expose it on `LibrarySource` and use it in the service, or drop it.

packages/rekordbox-library/src/identity..content: `storeWithLibrary` never seeds the `MemoryAliasStore`, and every lookup is served from the local `rows` map. Since `resolveTrackId` mints a brand-new id via `makeId` whenever the store has no matching alias, `resolveLiveTrack`'s alias-store integration is never actually exercised — these tests would still pass even if the store argument were ignored entirely. Seed the store with a known alias (e.g. `rekordbox:101 -> "T-101"`) and assert the exact returned `trackId` so wrong-row/path selection is caught.

`expect(r.trackId).not.toBeNull()` is tautological here: with an unseeded store the resolver always returns the `makeId()` value (`"t1"`), so this assertion can never fail even if a different/incorrect library row were selected. Assert the concrete id instead.

Same weak pattern for the path branch: `not.toBeNull()` cannot detect a wrong result. Additionally the path branch's documented confidence (0.7) is never asserted, so a drift there goes undetected. Assert `matchedStep === "title-path"`, `confidence === 0.7` and the resolved id/value.

The test name/theme promises "confidence per step", but only the memory-reader confidence (`1`) is ever asserted. The DS-22 confidences for `lighting-ipc-id` (0.95), `agent-api` (0.9) and `history-table` (0.8) are never checked, so a regression in the resolver's confidence table passes silently. Add per-step confidence assertions for these branches.

The history-miss case only asserts `trackId` is null. It does not verify `matchedStep` (should be null), `confidence` (0) or that the emitted `history-table` step reports `matched: false` with the "id not in history table" note. A false-positive match or wrong step attribution would therefore go undetected. Assert the full outcome object.

packages/rekordbox-library/src/index.ts.content: Data loss: `??` only falls back to `filePath` when `canonicalPath` is `null`/`undefined`. If `canonicalPath` is an empty string ("") — e.g. a DB row where the composite provider stringified a blank canonical path — `??` returns "", and the later `path !== ""` guard then drops it, discarding the valid `filePath` entirely. The track's location is silently lost. Fall back when `canonicalPath` is empty/blank, not only when nullish.
packages/rekordbox-library/src/index.ts.suggestion_code: const path = row.canonicalPath !== undefined && row.canonicalPath !== "" ? row.canonicalPath : row.filePath;

packages/rekordbox-library/src/index.ts.content: `rekordboxId` is declared required but is copied into the identity without any validation/trimming. Since §12 resolution starts at the native ID, an empty or whitespace-only `rekordboxId` yields an identity with no resolvable native ID downstream. Consider normalizing the value here (e.g. trim and reject empty) or documenting the caller contract that a non-empty ID must be supplied.
packages/rekordbox-library/src/index.ts.existing_code: const out: { rekordboxId: string; canonicalPath?: string; title?: string; artist?: string } = { rekordboxId: row.rekordboxId };

packages/rekordbox-live/src/contract-sui.content: The guard `check(provider.getStatus() !== undefined, ...)` only records a message; the very next line(s) then dereference the value unconditionally (`provider.getStatus().state`). If a provider ever returns `undefined` (the check exists precisely because that is considered possible), the suite throws here and aborts, discarding all accumulated `failures` — directly contradicting the module contract stated at the top of the file ("returns the failures it found instead of throwing"). Bind the status once and guard the dereference.
packages/rekordbox-live/src/contract-sui.suggestion_code:
const status = provider.getStatus();
    check(status !== undefined, "status missing after start");

packages/rekordbox-live/src/contract-sui.content: More generally, the suite body is not wrapped to catch exceptions. Any throw from `provider.start()`, `subject.loadTrack()`, `subject.advance()` or `subject.malformed()` (e.g. a real socket provider that fails to bind, or the intentionally-leaky subject throwing) escapes out of `runProviderContractSuite` instead of being appended to `failures`. The red-run test relies on the suite returning a non-empty list (`expect(failures.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`), so a throwing subject makes that test error rather than report the intended failure. Consider catching per-step and pushing a failure string.

This assertion does not actually exercise the bounded queue. `ProviderBase.emit()` already clamps `queueDepth` with `Math.min(1, this.queueDepth + 1)`, so for every provider in this package the value can never exceed 1 and the check is tautological; additionally the loop only advances virtual time and never feeds new updates, so for harnesses whose `advance()` emits nothing the depth is just a leftover from the earlier `loadTrack` and nothing is measured at all. A provider with a genuinely unbounded queue would not be caught. Drive a burst of updates without draining and then assert the bound.

The comment states deck 2 "must stay at generation 0 and not borrow deck 1's track", but the assertions only verify a state exists and that its title differs from "Generation A". A leaked `id`/`artist` from deck 1, or a wrong/borrowed generation on deck 2, goes undetected. Assert its own track identity (id/title/artist) rather than merely "not Generation A".
packages/rekordbox-live/src/contract-sui.suggestion_code: check(deckTwo?.track?.id === "gen-c" && deckTwo?.track?.title === "Deck Two", "deck 2 did not report its own track text");

packages/rekordbox-live/src/contract-sui.content: `onDeckState` and `onConnection` return unsubscribe functions (see `DJLiveProvider`), but both return values are discarded here. The listeners are never removed, so they survive `provider.stop()` and any reuse of the same provider instance accumulates callbacks, causing cross-suite contamination and a memory/resource leak. Keep the unsubscribers and invoke them when the suite finishes.
